definitions.explanation: The three-stroke radical (氵) derived from 水, used in kanji related to water or liquids.

examples.japanese: さんずい⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{漢字|かんじ}→漢字：09480_kanji⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{水|みず}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{関係|かんけい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ある。
examples.english: Kanji with the sanzui radical are related to water.

examples.japanese: さんずい⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{調|しら}べる→調べる：01213_shiraberu⟧。
examples.english: To look it up by the sanzui radical.

notes:
さんずい (氵) is the three-stroke water radical, derived from {水|みず}.

KANJI EXAMPLES:
- {海|うみ} (sea)
- {池|いけ} (pond)
- {泳|およ}ぐ (to swim)
- {洗|あら}う (to wash)
- {湖|みずうみ} (lake)
- {波|なみ} (wave)
- {汗|あせ} (sweat)

RADICAL NAME ORIGIN:
三 (three) + 水 (water) = さんずい, referring to the three strokes.

Most kanji with さんずい relate to water, liquids, or fluidity.
